detailed_description:
[Shot 1]0.0-10.0s. A photographed medium-wide full-body martial-arts exchange, at normal brisk speed, with both actors' heads, hands and boots visible. Warm directional canyon daylight illuminates pores, individual hair, heavy cotton folds and practical flexible armor. Keep the approved faces and tactile materials, with no beauty smoothing, waxy skin or plastic surfaces. The camera follows the supplied single smooth circling/tracking path, maintaining a clear side view of the attack line. No cuts, shakes, flashes or zooms conceal contact.
Begin already active in close boxing range, matching the depth bodies' opening guard rather than holding the reference photograph. Around0.13s <Subject 2> drives a compact RIGHT punch into <Subject 1>'s upper abdomen below his guarding elbow; the glove briefly lands and immediately snaps back. Only after contact, <Subject 1>'s trunk and pelvis travel away, knees flex and feet catch the displaced weight. The receiver continues moving after the hand has separated.
Around1.53s <Subject 1> steps back into range and snaps a LEFT straight at <Subject 2>'s cheek/upper guard. The fist retracts at once. <Subject 2>'s head and torso whip back after contact and his pelvis follows into a backward catching step and lowered stance. Preserve intervening short boxing footwork and parries from the guide; both actors watch and react independently.
Around3.70s <Subject 1> plants his LEFT support boot, chambers his RIGHT leg, drives a brief low kick into <Subject 2>'s forward upper thigh, bends the knee to withdraw, then lands. The struck leg yields, <Subject 2>'s pelvis is displaced sideways/back and a separate foot catches his weight. Around4.63s <Subject 1> adds a short LEFT jab into the guarding glove; the block gives a smaller recoil and the hands immediately separate.
Continue the guide's close guarded exchange and short evasions through6.9s, with real shoulder/hip rotation and individually stepping boots. Around7.40s <Subject 2> plants his RIGHT support boot and drives a LEFT front kick into <Subject 1>'s torso/low forearm guard. The sole contacts briefly, the knee immediately bends to retract and the kicking foot returns to the ground. <Subject 1>'s shoulders, torso and pelvis are pushed away together, forcing a hurried catching step and a second settling step. He never remains suspended while the kicker balances on one leg.
Around8.37s <Subject 2> snaps a LEFT jab into the recovering guard and withdraws; around9.27s he drives a RIGHT straight toward the cheek. <Subject 1> recoils only after the brief contact, loses his initial base, lowers and catches himself; both continue moving into the ending rather than resetting to the reference pose. Maintain the guide's overall trajectories and momentum chain without copying repeated mannequin stiffness.
Hands and feet touch only momentarily and then separate. No prolonged pushing, interlocked hands, held knees or grappling. A supporting sole stays on the ground while the other foot lifts, travels and lands. Knees and hips absorb the shifted weight; no rigid foot skating or whole-body hovering. Cloth, hair and a little grounded dust respond after body motion, without decorative shock waves. Preserve limb ownership and natural human anatomy. No transformations, energy beams, blood, new wounds, extra people, text or logos. The output remains a silent visual test.

Preserve the reference identity, age, facial proportions, skin tone, costume and lighting. Natural skin microtexture, subtle pores, varied roughness and realistic highlights; natural eyes, muscle tension and expressions. Avoid waxy or plastic skin, beauty smoothing and airbrushed faces. Preserve the requested camera behavior; realism does not require camera shake.
Execute only the specified choreography, attacks, defenses, powers and outcome. Preserve each actor's identity, weapon ownership, geography and accumulated damage. Physical chain for every exchange: anticipation, ground-supported propulsion through legs and hips, trajectory, visible contact or evasion, momentum transfer, displacement, reaction, recovery. A block redirects momentum; a miss carries inertia. Balance, friction, traction, gravity and center of mass govern motion. Reactions caused by impacts start after contact; anticipatory defenses remain allowed. Feet step, pivot, skid or drag visibly, never slide rigidly. Grapples require grip, tension and leverage; jumps require compression, takeoff, ballistic travel and landing. Cloth, hair and loose material follow bodies with delayed secondary motion; environmental response follows the impact. Keep attack lines, contact and body displacement readable in the requested camera. Continue motion between actions without automatic guard resets, freeze poses, teleporting, limb fusion or interpenetration. No artificial slow motion or speed ramps unless requested. No flashes, cuts or camera shake to conceal missing contact. Finish requested attacks before any subsequent dialogue, preserving the exact dialogue and requested audio. Do not invent extra opponents, injuries, dialogue or soundtracks. Follow the requested intensity and the character's established abilities.
